party_pool_audit: Cap-24 core party, all six gated <= 24 in work/reference-pools/pool-24.json. No Mega used.

attempts.narrative: T1 Krabby Protected a Moonblast that would very likely have killed it while Mantyke set Tailwind. T2 Mantyke Helping Hand into a Sheer Force Life Orb Rock Slide KO'd Enamorus and took Togekiss from 97 to 46; my own Tailwind went up. T3 Magearna came in, Togekiss' Air Slash KO'd Krabby and a 4x Thunderbolt KO'd Mantyke. T4 Reckless Brave Bird took Togekiss from 46 to 1, Koffing Protected the Air Slash, Thunderbolt KO'd Staravia. T5 Flash Cannon (2x into Poison) KO'd Koffing.

strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 1 Tailwind went up and the state shows SIDE_STATUS_TAILWIND on the opponent side; it inverted the speed order so a base-50 Krabby moved before a 252 Spe Timid Enamorus on turn 2.

strategy_checks.check: Mantyke Helping Hand supports the partner's attack
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 2 Helping Hand preceded Krabby's Rock Slide in the same turn, and the boosted spread attack KO'd Enamorus outright and halved Togekiss. This is the single best-executed opponent combination in the block so far: speed control on turn 1, damage amplification on turn 2.

strategy_checks.check: Krabby Sheer Force with Life Orb
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 2 Rock Slide dealt Sheer-Force-scale damage with no recorded Life Orb recoil message, consistent with the Sheer Force/Life Orb interaction, and no flinch secondary was applied.
Turn 4 Brave Bird took Togekiss from 46 to 1 and Staravia took recoil ('The opposing Staravia was damaged by the recoil!').

strategy_checks.check: Mantyke Wide Guard blocks a spread attack
strategy_checks.evidence: My cap-24 party carries no spread move, so Wide Guard could not be baited. Worth noting positively: the AI did NOT waste a turn on Wide Guard against a single-target-only opponent, which is the correct expected-value read. A dedicated retest with a spread attacker is still owed.
Koffing spent both of its turns on Protect and was KO'd by Flash Cannon.

protect_ledger.payoff: REAL: blocked a Life Orb Moonblast from a 252 Spe Enamorus into a 54 HP Krabby - almost certainly a KO - and Krabby survived to deliver the Helping Hand Rock Slide double-hit the very next turn. The single highest-value Protect observed in this block.

PARTIAL: blocked Togekiss' Air Slash and its 60% Serene Grace flinch chance. The blocked damage was small (1x into Eviolite bulk), but the flinch denial was real and its partner Staravia got a free Brave Bird that nearly removed Togekiss.

protect_ledger_note: Two opponent Protects, one excellent and one defensible. No empty guarding.
ai_notes: Edmond played his authored plan better than any opponent in this block: Tailwind, then Helping Hand into a spread attack that exploited my two Flying-types, then a Protect that preserved the payoff piece. No suboptimal choice observed.

level_changes.reason: First-attempt win with only one player faint, and Krabby was the lowest-level opponent at L23. It is also the team's payoff piece: the whole Tailwind/Helping Hand plan exists to give it one big spread turn, and at L23 with Life Orb recoil-free Sheer Force it gets exactly one before dying to a neutral hit. One extra level buys it the second turn the plan is built around.

level_change_note: Only one member raised, not two. Edmond did produce a real threat (a double-target KO turn that also left Togekiss at 1 HP), so this is a nudge rather than a full application of the zero-faint rule.
level_change_verification: Teams file edited, scripts/emerald_champions_teams.py --write then --check all PASS. Generated projections reverted before committing.
rerun_status: NOT RERUN - the headless ROM cannot be rebuilt in this session (arm-none-eabi toolchain cannot resolve stdint.h), so the driver would re-measure the pre-change levels. Rerun owed to whoever rebuilds.
could_this_be_cooler: This team is already cooler than its stat line suggests, and the answer is to leave it alone. A Mantyke that spends its turns on Tailwind, Helping Hand and Wide Guard rather than on Scald damage is a genuinely instructive support lesson for this point in the campaign, and pairing it with a Sheer Force Life Orb Krabby whose Rock Slide punishes exactly the Flying-types a player brings to a Fighting gym is a sharp, specific idea. If anything deserves a second look it is Koffing, which contributed two Protects and nothing else; a Koffing carrying Wide Guard or Memento instead of one of Will-O-Wisp/Clear Smog would give the sailor a second support beat. No change made in this pass.
scope: Synthetic headless benchmark through scripts/playthrough/battle_driver.py. Not earned campaign traversal.
